job.title: Farm Hand EOI - November
job.description:
Farm Hand - Expression of Interest (EOI)
Are you ready to start your career in the vibrant agriculture industry? We are seeking a reliable, energetic, and hardworking Farm Hand to join our client's team, working across poultry farms in the beautiful Far North Adelaide. This essential role offers an exciting opportunity to develop skills in a dynamic environment, contributing directly to the care and management of poultry livestock.
Role Overview:
As a Farm Hand, you will be hands-on with chickens, performing a variety of essential farm tasks. This role requires physical stamina, a positive attitude, and a commitment to safety. It’s ideal for those living near Elizabeth or northern Adelaide who are eager to enter the agriculture sector and grow their skills within a supportive team.
Required Skills:
  • Ability to work physically with ongoing manual handling up to 20kgs
  • Excellent physical fitness and stamina for repetitive tasks
  • Positive, energetic, and hardworking attitude
  • Strong focus on safety and adherence to safety protocols
  • Own vehicle and valid driver’s license
  • Willingness to work with live birds and perform farm duties
  • Demonstrated reliability and punctuality
  • Morning start times
Nice to Have Skills:
  • Previous farm or poultry experience (not mandatory)
  • Basic knowledge of safe work practices
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team
  • Basic literacy and numeracy skills
Preferred Education and Experience:
  • No formal education required; experience in manual labour or farm work is advantageous but not essential
  • Candidates with a strong work ethic and a positive mindset are highly encouraged to apply
Other Requirements:
  • Must have full-time work rights in Australia
  • Cannot live or have regular contact with birds or pigs due to quarantine restrictions
  • Available for a five-day work week, with occasional weekend shifts
  • Willingness to undertake comprehensive safety training and PPE use
  Join us in this rewarding role and get your foot in the door of the agriculture industry. If you’re ready to take on this exciting challenge, apply now and become part of a supportive team dedicated to growth and excellence!

job.title: Purchasing & Warehouse Officer
job.description:
Position: Purchasing & Warehouse Officer
Contract Duration: 6 months duration
Commencement: ASAP
Location: Kwinana, WA
Weekly Hours: Monday to Friday - 40 hours per week
Salary: $51.40 per hour (flat rate on all hours)


About the Position
The Purchasing & Warehouse Officer supports the efficient operation of the Warehouse through purchasing, inventory control, supply contract administration and distribution activities. Reporting to the Purchasing & Warehouse Supervisor, this role helps ensure the timely and cost-effective supply of material and equipment to support operational requirements.


Duties

  • Contribute to the efficient and effective daily operation of the Purchasing and Warehouse Management function
  • Receive, check, store, and issue maintenance parts and consumables
  • Pick and prepare parts / materials for planned maintenance and breakdown work
  • Inventory control, stocktaking and maintaining accurate stock records
  • Conduct Cyclic Reviews of inventory within Supply Stores
  • Identifying stock discrepancies
  • Maintain accurate transaction records
  • Liaise with Supplier Sales Representatives
  • Arrange for servicing and maintenance of equipment and plant
  • Complete and process all documentation for all issues and receipts including the return of stock, projects, direct supply and rotatable items.
  • Expediate purchase orders for stock items and direct supply, ensuring the end user is notified of the delivery and availability dates
  • Establish and maintain effective intra-divisional and cross-divisional working relationships
  • Safe operation of forklifts, pallet jacks and other materials-handling equipment where authorised
  • Work with maintenance supervisors, planners, and tradespeople to support timely availability of parts
  • Maintain good housekeeping and safe storage arrangements
  • Managing consumables, tools, spare parts and, where relevant, hazardous materials
  • Using computerised inventory, purchasing or maintenance-management systems

Qualifications & Experience

  • Demonstrated experience with warehouse management responsibilities relating to materials management
  • Demonstrated experience with computerised supply systems in relation to procurement, contract and materials management
  • Demonstrated experience in using PC applications and systems
  • Well-developed knowledge of supply practices and procedures and demonstrated ability to develop new and review existing procedures
  • Understanding of Accounts Payable practices and principles
  • Current “C” Class Drivers licence
  • Current “LF” Class Forklift Operators licence
  • Current “WP” Class high risk license (Boom type elevating work platform)
  • Intermediate Microsoft Excel skills

job.title: Principal Systems Engineer - Integration & Autonomous Systems
job.description:

Responsibilities may include:

  • Working closely with vendors, OEMs and multidisciplinary engineering teams
  • Supporting verification, validation and integration readiness activities
  • Resolving complex technical and integration challenges across multiple systems
  • Driving engineering governance, traceability and quality outcomes
  • Supporting deployment, operational readiness and continuous improvement initiatives
  • Providing technical leadership across safety-critical and mission-critical environments
About You

You will ideally come from a highly regulated and technically demanding engineering environment such as:
  • Aerospace
  • Defence
  • Automotive
  • Autonomous Systems
  • Rail
  • Robotics
  • Industrial Automation
  • Mining Technology
You will bring experience in one or more of the following areas:
  • Systems Engineering
  • Systems Integration
  • Verification & Validation (V&V)
  • Functional Safety
  • Requirements Management
  • Engineering Assurance
  • Technical Governance
  • Platform, Vehicle or Equipment Integration
  • Safety-Critical Systems
You will also demonstrate:
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
  • The ability to balance engineering rigour with practical delivery outcomes
  • Experience working with internal stakeholders, vendors and external partners
  • A collaborative approach with strong communication and leadership skills
Highly Regarded
  • Experience with HIL, SIL or simulation-based environments
  • Experience with embedded, control or autonomous systems

  • Experience within mining, defence, aerospace, automotive or industrial technology sectors

  • Collaborative team environment with strong technical leadership
If you are a systems-focused engineer who enjoys solving complex integration challenges and delivering real-world engineering outcomes, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Case Manager (Administrative Review Tribunal)
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Case Manager to manage a portfolio of complex review matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
This role requires a highly organised professional who can exercise sound judgement, navigate complex issues, and build strong stakeholder relationships. You will be responsible for the end-to-end management of cases, identifying resolution pathways, gathering and analysing information, and contributing to positive outcomes through effective case management and dispute resolution practices.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Manage end-to-end case management activities for matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART).
  • Analyse complex information and develop options to support early and effective resolution.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Obtain, assess, and interpret evidence to support decision-making and case outcomes.
  • Prepare high-quality briefs, correspondence, reports, and case management documentation.
  • Attend and participate in Case Conferences, Conciliations, and Hearings.
  • Apply negotiation, advocacy, and dispute resolution techniques to resolve matters efficiently.
  • Identify, assess, and respond to risks impacting participants, operational outcomes, and business objectives.
  • Manage competing priorities and meet legislated and operational timeframes.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and best-practice case management approaches.


You Must Have
 
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, sensitive, or high-risk cases.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to build effective working relationships.
  • Proven analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with the ability to make sound decisions.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing detailed reports, briefs, or recommendations.
  • Strong verbal communication, negotiation, and influencing skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume and deadline-driven environment.
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, or procedural frameworks.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to exercise professional judgement in complex situations.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team while managing an independent caseload
  • Experience with administrative law, merits review, tribunal, or appeals processes.
  • Experience within disability, health, community services, government, or social services environments.
  • Experience in insurance claims, underwriting, actuarial services, or compensation schemes.
  • Experience in dispute resolution, investigations, complaints handling, or regulatory case management.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Melbourne, VIC
  • $60.26 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 19th November 2026

job.title: Recruitment Consultant - Industrial
job.description:
Recruitment Consultant | Industrial

St Georges Terrace, Perth | Work with a National Client

Looking for a recruitment role where you can truly make an impact?

Join Chandler Macleod's Industrial team in our St Georges Terrace office and take ownership of recruitment activities for one of our key national clients. This is a fantastic opportunity to work alongside a highly supportive and experienced team while building strong relationships with candidates and stakeholders.

If you enjoy a fast-paced environment, thrive on delivering exceptional service, and want the opportunity to manage the full employee lifecycle from attraction through to onboarding and workforce support, we'd love to hear from you.

Why Join Us?
  • Prime CBD location with easy access to public transport, cafes and entertainment.
  • Work with one of our major national clients.
  • Supportive, collaborative and high-performing team culture.
  • Variety in your day with recruitment, onboarding, workforce management and safety responsibilities.
  • Career development opportunities within one of Australia's leading workforce solutions businesses.
  • Autonomy to manage your portfolio while being supported by experienced leaders.
About the Role

As a Recruitment Consultant, your primary objective is to deliver end-to-end recruitment solutions while supporting candidate engagement, workplace safety, attendance management and performance outcomes.
You will be responsible for sourcing and placing quality candidates, conducting workplace visits and inductions, supporting workforce compliance and ensuring exceptional service delivery to both clients and employees.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Recruitment
  • Source and attract candidates through advertising, networking, referrals and proactive talent sourcing.
  • Screen, interview and assess candidates against client requirements.
  • Build and maintain strong talent pipelines.
  • Manage the recruitment process from job brief through to placement.
  • Conduct reference checks and coordinate offers.
  • Maintain regular communication with candidates throughout the recruitment journey.
  • Provide advice regarding pay rates, workforce trends and career opportunities.
Candidate Management & Workforce Support
  • Monitor attendance and employee performance.
  • Maintain regular contact with on-hire workforce.
  • Address employee enquiries and provide ongoing support.
  • Investigate and resolve workplace issues and complaints.
  • Develop performance improvement plans where required.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies and procedures.
Inductions & Onboarding
  • Welcome and onboard new employees.
  • Conduct site inductions and workplace orientations.
  • Perform site walk-throughs and explain workplace expectations.
  • Ensure candidates understand safety procedures and client requirements.
  • Deliver a positive onboarding experience.
Safety & Compliance
  • Conduct regular safety observations and workplace visits.
  • Identify and report workplace hazards.
  • Support implementation of corrective actions.
  • Promote a strong safety-first culture.
  • Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety requirements.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
  • Previous experience in recruitment, labour hire, account management or a sales-focused environment
  • Strong relationship-building and stakeholder management skills
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities
  • Proven ability to work in a target-driven environment
  • Exceptional organisational and administrative skills
  • Sound computer literacy and experience with CRM or recruitment systems.
  • Strong problem-solving and negotiation skills
  • A commitment to workplace safety and compliance
  • High levels of integrity, professionalism and accountability
  • The ability to work independently while contributing to a collaborative team culture

Ready for Your Next Challenge?
If you're looking for a recruitment role that offers variety, ownership, a great team and the chance to grow your career with one of Australia's leading workforce solutions businesses, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now and take the next step in your recruitment career with Chandler Macleod. Contact Jo Ellerman (02) 66919106 for a confidential chat and a copy of the PD

job.title: Project Delivery Manager – Commercial Projects
job.description:
Project Delivery Manager – Commercial Projects

Beresfield, Newcastle NSW | $95–$105 per hour + Super | Temp-to-Perm Opportunity 
  • $95–$105 per hour + super with genuine permanent career prospects

  • Lead a diverse portfolio of 30+ commercial projects valued up to $1.2 million

  • Predominantly office-based leadership role with an established, supportive team

About the opportunity Chandler Macleod is partnering with a well-established Australian business specialising in premium commercial washroom systems to recruit an experienced Project Delivery Manager for an immediate opportunity based in Beresfield.

Our client designs and supplies innovative commercial washroom solutions for major developments across Australia, including airports, commercial towers, retail environments and infrastructure projects.

With approximately 30 projects currently underway, the business is seeking a commercially focused professional to oversee project delivery, lead internal teams and ensure projects are completed efficiently, profitably and to a high standard.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Project Manager, Project Delivery Manager or commercially minded Operations Manager looking to take ownership of a diverse project portfolio.

A traditional construction background is not essential. We welcome applications from professionals with relevant experience across manufacturing, engineering, commercial products, fit-out and supply-and-install environments.

About the role Reporting directly to the Managing Director, you will oversee the commercial and operational delivery of multiple concurrent projects.

Projects typically range in value from $40,000 to $450,000, with larger projects reaching approximately $1.2 million.

You will manage the full project lifecycle, from contract award through manufacturing, dispatch, installation, practical completion and financial close-out.

With established production, procurement, project administration and site teams already in place, your focus will be on commercial management, operational coordination and ensuring projects remain on schedule and within budget.

  • Oversee the end-to-end delivery of multiple concurrent commercial projects.

  • Manage project schedules, budgets, milestones, risks and deliverables.

  • Lead and coordinate internal Project Management, Procurement, Administration, Site Management and After Sales functions.

  • Coordinate manufacturing, workshop, dispatch and installation activities to meet project timelines.

  • Manage relationships with clients, head contractors, installation subcontractors and suppliers.

  • Monitor project costs, margins and commercial performance, ensuring effective financial close-out.

  • Review drawings, specifications and technical documentation to support accurate project delivery.

  • Resolve delivery challenges and implement practical, commercially sound solutions.

  • Ensure appropriate WHS, quality and subcontractor compliance requirements are maintained.

  • Maintain accurate project reporting and improve operational systems, workflows and processes.

  • Provide regular project performance updates to senior management.

About you We are seeking a confident, organised and commercially astute professional who enjoys managing multiple projects, coordinating teams and delivering successful outcomes.

To be successful, you will have:

  • Demonstrated experience in project management, project delivery or operational management.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.

  • Strong commercial acumen, including budgeting, cost control and financial reporting.

  • Experience coordinating internal teams, external suppliers and subcontractors.

  • Excellent organisational, planning and problem-solving capabilities.

  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.

  • Ability to interpret project drawings, specifications and technical documentation.

  • Confidence working with project management systems, spreadsheets and reporting tools.

  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach and strong attention to detail.

  • Current driver's licence – mandatory.

Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Experience managing variations, progress claims, retentions and security of payment requirements.

  • Qualifications in Project Management, Engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline.

  • Experience implementing process improvements, reporting systems or workflow automation.

What's on offer?
  • $95–$105 per hour + superannuation, depending on experience.

  • Immediate start with a genuine temporary-to-permanent opportunity.

  • Company vehicle included as part of the permanent employment offering.

  • Predominantly office-based position in Beresfield, with occasional site visits.

  • Exposure to a diverse portfolio of commercial projects across Australia.

  • Opportunity to contribute directly to business performance and operational improvements.

  • Long-term career prospects within an established and growing business.

job.title: Internal Review Officer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Agency's External Review team manages matters before the Administrative Review Tribunal (ART), with a focus on resolving disputes in a fair, consistent, and timely manner. The team works closely with participants, representatives, legal practitioners, and internal stakeholders to support effective outcomes while balancing legislative obligations and operational priorities.
Operating in a fast-paced environment, the team manages complex and sensitive matters and plays an important role in improving the experience of individuals engaging with the review process.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Internal Review Officer to undertake reviews of decisions relating to participant access, eligibility, and funded supports.
This role is suited to professionals who enjoy analysing complex information, interpreting legislation and policy, and making evidence-based recommendations. You will manage a caseload of review matters while ensuring decisions are completed accurately, within required timeframes, and in line with legislative and operational requirements.
The successful candidate will demonstrate strong analytical skills, attention to detail, sound judgement, and a commitment to delivering participant-focused outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Undertake internal reviews by gathering, assessing, and analysing information and evidence.
  • Apply relevant legislation, policy, operational guidelines, and procedures to support fair and consistent recommendations.
  • Prepare clear, objective, and well-reasoned review findings and recommendations.
  • Communicate review outcomes, review rights, and appeal pathways in a professional and timely manner.
  • Engage with participants, representatives, and stakeholders to obtain information and support informed decision-making.
  • Manage a caseload of review matters while meeting legislative and operational timeframes.
  • Maintain accurate records and documentation to support compliant and defensible review processes.
  • Apply person-centred, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive approaches when dealing with sensitive matters.
  • Contribute to quality assurance activities, continuous improvement initiatives, and service delivery enhancements.
  • Maintain knowledge of relevant legislation, policy, and operational frameworks.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience interpreting and applying legislation, policy, procedures, or regulatory frameworks.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyse information and evidence to develop logical, balanced, and defensible recommendations.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to make sound decisions based on available information.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing reports, findings, recommendations, or assessments.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to communicate complex information clearly and professionally.
  • Experience managing competing priorities and caseloads within established timeframes.
  • Ability to manage sensitive or complex matters using sound judgement and professionalism.
  • Strong organisational skills and experience maintaining accurate records and case documentation.
  • Commitment to delivering participant-focused outcomes and high-quality customer service.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment while managing individual responsibilities.

Highly Desirable
  • Experience within government, administrative review, regulatory, disability, health, community services, or human services environments.
  • Knowledge of administrative review processes and evidence-based decision-making.
  • Experience assessing complex information and preparing recommendations in a legislative or policy-driven environment.
  • Knowledge of disability, functional impact, or participant-centred service delivery models.
  • Experience using case management, customer relationship management (CRM), or workflow management systems.
  • Qualifications in Law, Public Administration, Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, Disability Studies, or a related discipline.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Melbourne, VIC
  • $55.24 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.



Application closes on the 19th November 2026

Reporting within the Asset Management function, you will be responsible for driving asset management practices across the organisation, supporting long-term planning, and ensuring asset data, frameworks and processes align with industry best practice.

job.title: GIS Technician
job.description:
About the Role
In this position, you will lead the development, management, and analysis of spatial data to support environmental projects, policy development, and operational programs. You will work across multiple stakeholders to deliver accurate mapping, spatial insights, technical reports, and innovative GIS solutions.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop, maintain, and enhance GIS datasets, web mapping applications, and spatial products.
  • Produce high-quality maps, dashboards, analysis, and technical reports to support environmental and regulatory programs.
  • Manage end-to-end spatial projects, ensuring delivery within agreed timelines and quality standards.
  • Design and improve spatial data capture processes, standards, and workflows.
  • Provide expert technical advice on GIS technologies, spatial analysis, and data management.
  • Collaborate with government agencies, internal teams, and external stakeholders to exchange and manage large spatial datasets.
  • Support evidence-based decision-making through research, data interpretation, and analytical insights.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and emerging GIS technologies.
About You
To be successful, you will bring:
  • Strong experience using ESRI technologies, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and ESRI Web Applications.
  • Expertise in spatial data management, analysis, visualisation, and quality assurance processes.
  • Experience designing and supporting field data collection solutions and user-focused GIS applications.
  • Knowledge of spatial databases and geospatial data workflows.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences.
Desirable Skills
  • Experience with FME Workbench or similar data integration and automation tools.
  • Advanced capability in Microsoft Power BI and Excel for reporting and analytics.
  • Knowledge of environmental, ecological, natural resource, or sustainability datasets.
  • Experience working with government agencies or regulatory environments.
 
If you're passionate about spatial technology and want to use your GIS expertise to help shape environmental outcomes, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Manager Integration and Planning (Transport Planner)
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Manager Integration and Planning (Transport Planner) to support transport integration, strategic planning, and stakeholder coordination activities for a nationally significant infrastructure program. This is an excellent opportunity for a planning professional with experience in transport, infrastructure, or major project environments to contribute to complex network planning and development initiatives.

Based in Sydney, Canberra or Newcastle, you will work closely with government stakeholders, multidisciplinary project teams, consultants, and senior decision-makers to coordinate planning activities, technical investigations, and strategic transport integration initiatives.

Contract Details
  • Location: Sydney, Canberra or Newcastle
  • Contract Duration: 12 Months (with potential extension)
  • Hours: 37.5 hours per week
  • Work Authorization: Australian Citizen ONLY

Key Responsibilities
  • Coordinate transport integration and planning activities across major infrastructure projects.
  • Manage planning initiatives relating to station access, interchange functionality, multimodal connectivity and transport network interfaces.
  • Support strategic planning, network development and infrastructure integration investigations.
  • Coordinate technical inputs from consultants, advisers, internal teams and external stakeholders.
  • Review planning and design deliverables to ensure alignment with project objectives and requirements.
  • Prepare reports, executive briefings, governance papers and presentations for senior stakeholders.
  • Monitor project schedules, budgets, risks, issues, dependencies and progress reporting.
  • Support engagement with government agencies, local councils, transport operators and industry stakeholders.
  • Undertake research and analysis to inform planning recommendations and decision-making.
  • Contribute to the successful delivery of strategic transport and infrastructure outcomes.

About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Degree qualification in Transport Planning, Urban & Regional Planning, Engineering, Infrastructure Planning, Geography or a related discipline.
  • Experience within transport planning, infrastructure planning or major project delivery environments.
  • Strong project management and coordination skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Experience working with government stakeholders, consultants and multidisciplinary project teams.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, facilitation and relationship management capabilities.
  • Ability to review and interpret technical information and communicate findings clearly to diverse audiences.
  • Experience preparing reports, briefings, presentations and governance documentation.
  • Experience in rail, public transport or major infrastructure projects will be highly regarded.
  • Postgraduate qualifications in a relevant discipline will be advantageous.

If this sounds like you, we encourage you to APPLY now.

If you are a planning or infrastructure professional who thrives in complex project environments and enjoys working with diverse stakeholders to deliver strategic outcomes, apply now through Chandler Macleod.

job.title: Logistics Engineering Specialist
job.description:
Brisbane, QLD | Hybrid | 6‑Month Contract

An opportunity is available for a Logistics Engineering Specialist to support Defence sustainment and product support activities across complex capability programs.
This role suits professionals with experience in Integrated Logistics Support (ILS), Integrated Product Support (IPS), supportability, reliability or sustainment engineering, who enjoy analysing technical data, identifying improvement opportunities, and contributing to long-term capability outcomes.


The Role:

You’ll work in a product support environment, helping improve equipment performance, availability and supportability through analysis of maintenance, engineering and operational data.


Key responsibilities include:
  • Review, validate and analyse data from multiple technical and operational sources
  • Identify trends, recurring failures, supportability issues and opportunities for improvement
  • Support reliability, maintainability and sustainment improvement activities
  • Assist with logistics engineering and product support activities across acquisition and in-service programs
  • Contribute to ILS / IPS deliverables and supporting documentation
  • Prepare reports, recommendations and technical outputs for stakeholders
  • Collaborate with engineering, maintenance, supply chain and project teams

About You
You may come from a background in:
  • Logistics Engineering
  • Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) / Integrated Product Support (IPS)
  • Supportability Engineering
  • Reliability Engineering / RAM
  • Product Support / Sustainment Engineering
  • Systems Engineering with sustainment exposure

Experience we’re looking for:
  • Defence acquisition and/or sustainment experience
  • Experience analysing engineering, maintenance, reliability and/or operational data
  • Knowledge of logistics engineering and supportability disciplines
  • Experience working with technical documentation and engineering data
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capability
  • Ability to produce clear, evidence-based recommendations and outputs

Highly regarded:
  • LSAR experience
  • FRACAS exposure
  • Reliability or RAM analysis
  • Maintenance Task Analysis (MTA)
  • FMECA / FMEA
  • LORA
  • Aviation, aerospace or uncrewed systems experience
  • Current Defence security clearance

Requirements:
  • Australian Citizenship (required due to security clearance requirements)
  • Currently hold or have ability to obtain and maintain an AGSVA security clearance (Baseline Level)
  • Ability to work in Brisbane in a hybrid environment
  • Start in November

Candidates will be reviewed as received, for a copy of the position description and further details, please call 07 2140 6649.

job.title: Picker
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is currently seeking reliable and motivated Warehouse Voice Pickers to join the team at a national beverage supplier in Eastern Creek. These are fantastic opportunities for people who enjoy staying active, working in a fast-paced environment, and being part of a supportive team.

As a Voice Picker, you'll play an important role in the order fulfilment process, ensuring customer orders are picked accurately and safely while meeting productivity targets.

Training is provided, and you'll be joining a team that values safety, teamwork and diversity.

If you're ready for ongoing work with a great team and excellent training opportunities, apply now!

job.title: Senior Service Designer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The Service Design team works closely with stakeholders to improve services, processes, and experiences for customers. The team focuses on identifying opportunities to simplify and enhance service delivery by understanding user needs, analysing business processes, and designing practical improvements that deliver better outcomes.
Working across policy, operations, technology, and business functions, the team drives continuous improvement initiatives that improve efficiency, consistency, and customer experience

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Process Improvement Specialist to lead and support complex business improvement initiatives across a large and dynamic operating environment.
This role will focus on understanding current processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, analysing operational data, and designing practical solutions that enhance service delivery and customer outcomes.
Working closely with business stakeholders, service designers, business analysts, and operational teams, you will play a key role in shaping future processes and supporting the delivery of continuous improvement initiatives.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex business problems, engaging with stakeholders, and driving meaningful change.

Key Responsibilities
  • Analyse and map current business processes and customer journeys.
  • Identify inefficiencies, risks, bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Facilitate workshops and stakeholder engagement sessions to gather insights and requirements.
  • Conduct operational analysis, including time and motion studies and process reviews.
  • Collect, interpret, and analyse data from a variety of sources to support decision-making.
  • Develop recommendations to improve business processes, customer experiences, and operational performance.
  • Collaborate with service designers, business analysts, project teams, and business stakeholders to design and deliver effective solutions.
  • Support testing and evaluation activities to measure the effectiveness of process improvements.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and maintain improvement backlogs.
  • Provide guidance and coaching to team members on process improvement methods and best practices.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience in service design, customer experience, or human-centred design.
  • Experience conducting time and motion studies.
  • Experience within government, health, disability, insurance, banking, or other large service delivery organisations.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, Continuous Improvement, or Business Process Management experience.
  • Experience working on transformation or organisational change programs.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • $602.55 daily + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

Application closes on the 15 November 2026

job.title: Procurement Specialist
job.description:
Procurement Specialist - Capital

Location: Pinjarra
Duration: 12-Month Contract (Potential Extension)
Rate: Competitive Hourly Rate + Super

Procurement Specialist - Capital Projects
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Procurement Specialist to join a leading global resources organisation, supporting the delivery of major capital projects across Western Australia.

Reporting to the Procurement Manager - Capital, you will be the key procurement lead responsible for managing sourcing, contract negotiations, supplier performance, and procurement strategy execution across multiple capital projects. Working closely with engineering, project delivery and operational stakeholders, you will ensure critical equipment, materials and services are delivered safely, efficiently, and in line with project schedules and budgets.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and execute procurement strategies for major capital projects.
  • Lead RFIs, RFPs, supplier evaluations and contract negotiations.
  • Manage supplier relationships, performance and contractual obligations.
  • Ensure goods and services are delivered on time, within specification and budget.
  • Identify and deliver cost-saving and process improvement opportunities.
  • Monitor procurement risks and implement mitigation strategies.
  • Provide procurement guidance to project teams and stakeholders.
  • Ensure compliance with company policies, governance standards and procurement procedures.
About You
  • Proven experience in capital project procurement within mining, resources, energy, manufacturing or heavy industry.
  • Strong contract negotiation and supplier management capability.
  • Experience managing complex sourcing activities and high-value procurement packages.
  • Ability to influence stakeholders across engineering, project delivery and operational teams.
  • Strong commercial acumen with a focus on value creation and risk management.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills.
This role offers the opportunity to contribute to major capital projects while working with a highly regarded procurement team in a large-scale industrial environment.

Apply now or contact Chandler Macleod for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Merchandiser - Mansfield
job.description:

Chandler Macleod is seeking motivated individuals to join our team as Casual Merchandisers for our valued client, Tip Top Bakeries – Australia’s leading bakery products manufacturer.

Key Responsibilities
  • Visiting local supermarkets to merchandise bakery products
  • Following planograms to stock shelves
  • Checking and rotating stock, removing expired or damaged items
  • Maintaining a clean and tidy product display
  • Completing basic paperwork as required
  • Ensuring products such as bread, muffins, and crumpets are well presented and available for customers
What’s on Offer
✨ Ongoing flexible casual work with a trusted national brand
✨ Great hourly rate
✨ Opportunity to work close to home
✨ Comprehensive face-to-face training provided
✨ Pathway to a permanent role for the right candidate

job.title: Complaints Officer
job.description:
Complaints Officer
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for experienced and resilient Complaints Officers to join a high-performing team responsible for managing complex complaints and supporting positive outcomes for participants.

This is an excellent opportunity for professionals with complaints handling, case management, investigations, customer resolution, or government administration experience who are passionate about delivering quality service and navigating complex matters with empathy and professionalism. 

About the Role
As a Complaints Officer, you will play a critical role in managing and resolving escalated complaints, ensuring matters are handled in accordance with relevant legislation, policies, and service standards. You will engage with a broad range of stakeholders while maintaining a strong focus on quality outcomes and timely resolutions.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage and assess complaints, including investigating issues, recording information, resolving matters, and making referrals where required. 
  • Handle escalated and sensitive matters while ensuring strict service deadlines are achieved.
  • Communicate with customers, representatives, and internal stakeholders through professional written correspondence and outbound calls. 
  • Maintain accurate records and case notes within organisational systems.
  • Assess information, identify risks, and follow appropriate escalation processes where required. 
  • Prepare reports and documentation to support decision-making, governance, and compliance requirements. 

About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Experience managing complaints, investigations, case management, customer resolutions, or similar functions. 
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage professionally with diverse stakeholders.
  • The ability to interpret and apply legislation, policies, and procedures. 
  • Excellent organisational skills and the capacity to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment. 
  • Resilience, sound judgement, and the ability to work with sensitive and potentially distressing information. 
  • A genuine commitment to delivering high-quality customer outcomes and supporting people from diverse backgrounds. 

Benefits
  • APS5 equivalent  level opportunity
  • Multiple locations - Geelong/ Broadmeadows/ Richmond/ Chermside / Newcastle
  • Meaningful work that contributes to improved participant experiences
  • Supportive team environment
  • Hybrid working arrangements available

job.title: Senior Service Designer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Role
The Agency is seeking an experienced Process Improvement Specialist to lead and support complex business improvement initiatives across a large and dynamic operating environment.
This role will focus on understanding current processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, analysing operational data, and designing practical solutions that enhance service delivery and customer outcomes.
Working closely with business stakeholders, service designers, business analysts, and operational teams, you will play a key role in shaping future processes and supporting the delivery of continuous improvement initiatives.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex business problems, engaging with stakeholders, and driving meaningful change.

Key Responsibilities
  • Analyse and map current business processes and customer journeys.
  • Identify inefficiencies, risks, bottlenecks, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Facilitate workshops and stakeholder engagement sessions to gather insights and requirements.
  • Conduct operational analysis, including time and motion studies and process reviews.
  • Collect, interpret, and analyse data from a variety of sources to support decision-making.
  • Develop recommendations to improve business processes, customer experiences, and operational performance.
  • Collaborate with service designers, business analysts, project teams, and business stakeholders to design and deliver effective solutions.
  • Support testing and evaluation activities to measure the effectiveness of process improvements.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives and maintain improvement backlogs.
  • Provide guidance and coaching to team members on process improvement methods and best practices.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience in service design, customer experience, or human-centred design.
  • Experience conducting time and motion studies.
  • Experience within government, health, disability, insurance, banking, or other large service delivery organisations.
  • Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, Continuous Improvement, or Business Process Management experience.
  • Experience working on transformation or organisational change programs.

Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Nationwide
  • $602.55 daily + Super

Chandler Macleod is partnering with a well-established regional business servicing the food manufacturing, fresh produce and food distribution sectors to recruit an experienced Branch Manager based in Bendigo, Victoria.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced operations leader who thrives in fast-paced environments and understands the demands of food-related operations. With a strong focus on inventory control, quality standards, compliance and customer service, you will be responsible for the overall performance of the branch while leading a diverse operational team.

Whether your background is in food manufacturing, food processing, wholesale food distribution, fresh produce, FMCG or industrial operations, this role offers the opportunity to lead a high-performing site and drive operational excellence.

Reporting to senior leadership, the Branch Manager will be responsible for:

  • Distribution Centre Managers
  • Warehouse Managers

If you're an operational leader with experience in food manufacturing, food processing, fresh produce or FMCG environments and are looking for an opportunity to make a significant impact within a growing regional business, we'd love to hear from you.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a well-established organisation where quality, service and operational excellence are at the heart of everything they do.

job.title: Production Worker| Food Manufacturing | Multiple Locations
job.description:
Production Workers | Food Manufacturing | Western Suburbs

Ravenhall | Laverton North | Altona North
Morning, afternoon and night shift opportunities

Have experience in food production or processing? Chandler Macleod is seeking reliable and motivated Production Workers to join busy food manufacturing sites across Melbourne’s western suburbs.

Previous food production or food processing experience is essential. Please review the requirements for each location below.

Available Opportunities

Ravenhall – Food Production Workers
Morning and afternoon shifts | Opportunity to develop your skills

We’re looking for mechanically minded production workers who are keen to learn, with the potential to develop into operator roles.
  • Morning shift: 5:30am start
  • Afternoon shift: 1:45pm start
  • Previous food production or processing experience required
  • Mechanically minded, with an interest in learning production equipment
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow instructions
  • No food allergies due to exposure to food ingredients on site
Laverton North – Poultry Production Workers
Morning and afternoon shifts | Potential for permanent employment

These roles involve processing and packing raw chicken in a cold, fast-paced production environment.
  • Morning and afternoon shifts available, with varied start times depending on the area you are rostered to work in
  • Must be available to work across all seven days of the week
  • Initially approximately three shifts per week, with potential for additional shifts from the end of October
  • Opportunity to move into permanent employment after 3–4 months for the right candidates
  • Previous food production or processing experience required
  • Must be comfortable handling raw chicken and working in a cold environment
  • Full Australian working rights, a current driver’s licence and your own car are essential
Altona North – Bakery & Pastry Production Workers
Ad hoc morning and night shifts

Join a busy food manufacturing environment producing bakery and pastry goods. These opportunities suit experienced food production workers who are flexible and available to work shifts as required.
  • Morning and night shifts available
  • Ad hoc shifts, with work offered according to production requirements

job.title: Contracting Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Contracting Officer to support the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.
You will join a fast-paced, high-profile environment where your procurement and contracting expertise will directly support complex, strategically significant outcomes across the nuclear-powered submarine program.

About the Role
Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the APS6 Contracting Officer is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing specialist procurement and contracting advice and end-to-end support across procurement planning, market approaches, contract establishment and contract management.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will strengthen Australia’s national security and deliver lasting economic and industrial benefits for generations to come.
In this role, you will manage complex procurement and contract management activities while ensuring compliance with relevant legislation, policies and the Commonwealth procurement framework. You will provide practical, risk-informed commercial advice and develop solutions to complex procurement challenges.

About the Team
The Commercial Branch delivers end-to-end procurement, contracting and commercial support across the Australian Submarine Agency, enabling the successful delivery of Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine program.
You will join a professional and collaborative team that values innovation, integrity and continuous improvement, and works closely with stakeholders across the Agency to deliver compliant, value-for-money, strategically aligned procurement outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for supporting and delivering procurement and contracting outcomes, including:
  • Providing specialist procurement and contracting advice to support complex, strategically significant outcomes
  • Supporting procurement planning and commercial strategy development
  • Drafting approaches to market, supporting evaluations, and contributing to negotiations through to contract execution
  • Managing contract formation and ongoing contract management activities
  • Reviewing contract change proposals and commercial deliverables, and advising on performance outcomes
  • Identifying, assessing and advising on commercial risks and contractual matters
  • Providing practical, policy-aligned advice across procurement legislation, frameworks and best practice
  • Building and maintaining strong relationships with internal stakeholders, and engaging with legal and finance advisers as required
  • Supporting capability uplift and continuous improvement across procurement/commercial practices
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Experience managing complex procurements end-to-end (strategy, approach to market, evaluation, negotiation, contract execution)
  • Experience providing commercial support across contract management (performance, change, remediation)
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and sound judgement
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with an ability to tailor advice for different audiences
  • Ability to work strategically in a sensitive, fast-paced environment with competing priorities
  • Proven ability to build and sustain effective stakeholder relationships
  • Adaptability, resilience and flexibility in a changing environment
  • Sound understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Framework
Security Requirement
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance.

Location / Work Arrangement
  • Locations may include: Canberra ACT, Melbourne VIC, Port Adelaide SA, Rockingham WA
  • On-site work arrangements apply, with flexibility considered in line with operational and business requirements
Apply Now
If you are an experienced procurement and contracting professional seeking to contribute to a once-in-a-lifetime national program, we encourage you to apply today.

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines,  to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now
If you are an experienced Engineer looking to apply your expertise to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today. Please submit your current resume. Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at: https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Finance Business Partner to join the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

Working within the ASA environment, the APS6 Finance Business Partner is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing strategic financial analysis, assurance and advice to support the delivery of budgets and outcomes, including across the capability development process.

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia’s most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced APS6 Finance Business Partner to join the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
Working within the ASA environment, the APS6 Finance Business Partner is accountable (under broad direction and with a high degree of autonomy) for providing strategic financial analysis, assurance and advice to support the delivery of budgets and outcomes, including across the capability development process.

The acquisition of conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.
Within the ASA Finance Branch, you will support agency and program-wide decision-making through the development and implementation of processes that enable accurate, timely financial information and insight in a complex, fast-paced, high-profile environment.

About the Team
The ASA Finance Branch supports the Chief Financial Officer, the Assistant Director General Program Costing, and the broader ASA through the provision of expert strategic support and advice relating to the acquisition, sustainment and disposal of nuclear-powered submarines (NPS).
ASA fosters an inclusive culture that emphasises respect and collaboration and prioritises safety and security. You will be working at the cutting edge of capability delivery, supported by professionalisation pathways and unique career opportunities.

Key Responsibilities
You will be responsible for supporting and delivering finance business partnering outcomes, including:
  • Providing strategic financial analysis, assurance and advice to support budgets, outcomes and capability delivery
  • Developing and maintaining collaborative finance business partnerships, including identifying financial risks and opportunities
  • Supporting business leads with budget proposals and performance reviews, including assessing contracts/agreements for financial impacts against schedule
  • Contributing to financial aspects of asset management (e.g., asset reconciliations, Asset Valuation Models (AVMs), Project Capitalisation Plans, asset rollouts, aged/uncleared balances)
  • Preparing high-quality briefs and reports that identify issues and provide practical recommendations
  • Working within relevant Commonwealth financial and budgeting frameworks, legislation, policy and processes
  • Managing competing priorities while exercising initiative and judgement to achieve outcomes
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Proven experience providing strategic financial advice and analysis in complex stakeholder environments
  • Strong collaboration and relationship-building skills (you can partner effectively with senior stakeholders)
  • Sound understanding of commercial cost drivers and the financial impacts on deliverables
  • Experience preparing briefs, reports and recommendations to support decision-making
  • Ability to work independently with autonomy, initiative and accountability in a high-paced environment
Mandatory qualifications / experience (required)
Relevant experience as a Finance Business Partner / Finance Adviser (APS6 level or equivalent), ideally within government or similarly complex environments.

Security Requirement
Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance.
Flexible working arrangements may be supported where aligned with operational and business requirements.

Locations: Adelaide SA, Canberra ACT, Sydney NSW

job.title: Engineering Specialists – Multiple Disciplines | APS 6, EL1 & EL2
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for exceptional opportunities within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting one of Australia’s most significant long-term defence capability programs.

We are seeking experienced Engineers from a wide range of disciplines, at APS 6, Executive Level 1 and Executive Level 2, to contribute to a major naval defence capability program that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
This major naval defence capability program is a historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort brings together government, industry and international partners to deliver one of the most complex engineering programs in the nation’s history.

Engineers will work across technical governance, assurance, certification, design review and through-life support of advanced naval platforms and systems. Roles range from highly specialist to broad, depending on your discipline and experience, and you may have the opportunity to work across streams. Successful candidates may also have the opportunity to nominate for international placements with overseas partner organisations, with in-country training and support provided beforehand.

These positions attract a competitive remuneration package, including an additional premium for critical capability disciplines and generous superannuation.

About the Team
You’ll join engineering branches responsible for the technical governance, safety certification and objective quality evidence (OQE) that underpin the safe, effective and sovereign operation of Australia’s future naval capability. Teams combine civilian and military personnel from diverse disciplines, and the culture puts people, technical development, integrity and safety first.

Engineering Disciplines
We are interested in hearing from Engineers with experience in one or more of the following:

  • Mechanical, structural and materials engineering (including FEA and structural/materials modelling)
  • Electrical, electronic and mechatronic engineering
  • Instrumentation and control
  • Systems engineering and systems integration
  • Power, propulsion and energy systems
  • Safety case development, system safety and environmental protection
  • Marine structures, naval architecture, weld design and shock/survivability
  • Signature management (acoustic and non-acoustic), trials, measurement and analysis
  • Modelling and simulation (structural, thermal-hydraulics, fluid-structure interaction)
  • Field support, engineering investigations, and decommissioning and disposal
Key Responsibilities
Depending on level and discipline, responsibilities may include:

  • Reviewing, evaluating and recommending courses of action on designs, specifications and deviations to support approval and certification decisions
  • Developing the methodologies, processes and OQE used to assure and certify engineering systems
  • Contributing to safety cases, regulatory submissions, and plans, processes and procedures
  • Working with national and international partners, industry, regulators and academia to apply engineering best practice
  • Participating in international meetings and workshops, sometimes outside standard Australian working hours
  • Preparing high-quality briefs, reports and presentations to inform senior decision-makers
  • At EL1 and EL2, leading teams, planning and managing technical programs and resources, and mentoring developing engineers
About You
You will demonstrate:

  • A Bachelor of Engineering (or equivalent) that satisfies the Washington Accord for recognition as a Professional Engineer
  • Strong technical competence in your discipline and a willingness to keep learning alongside leading experts in novel technologies
  • Sound judgement and a systems-thinking approach to identifying and managing risk
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to a range of audiences
  • The ability to build effective relationships across government, industry and international stakeholders
  • For EL1 and EL2 roles, demonstrated leadership, supervision and mentoring experience
Highly regarded but not essential:

  • Chartered Professional Engineer (Engineers Australia), Registered Professional Engineer (Professionals Australia), or membership of an equivalent institution such as RINA, IMechE, IMarEST or IEEE (or the ability to obtain it within 12 months)
  • Experience in Defence, defence industry, maritime, energy or other highly regulated, safety-critical sectors
  • Experience working with overseas partners or within multi-regulator environments
  • Openness to an international placement of 2 to 3 years
You don’t need Defence experience. Engineers from all applicable industries are encouraged to apply.

Locations: Adelaide / Port Adelaide – SA, Canberra – ACT, Melbourne – VIC, Perth – WA, Sydney – NSW
 

Security Requirement
Applicants must be Australian citizens and able to obtain and maintain a minimum Negative Vetting Level 1 (NV1) security clearance. Some roles may require a higher clearance level.

Apply Now
If you are an experienced Engineer looking to apply your expertise to a once-in-a-generation national program, we encourage you to apply today. Please submit your current resume. Shortlisted candidates may be asked for a short statement (up to 600 words) on how their skills, knowledge and experience fit their chosen discipline.

This is a unique chance for an experienced EL2 Director Infrastructure Operations to join the Australian Submarine Agency (ASA), contributing to a nationally significant defence initiative that will shape Australia’s security, workforce, industrial capability and supply chains for decades to come.

About the Role
Working within the Australian Submarine Agency environment, the EL2 Director Infrastructure Operations will lead a critical function within the Infrastructure Planning, Performance and Integration (IPPI) team, supporting the delivery of a complex, nationally significant infrastructure portfolio.

The acquisition of conventionally-armed, nuclear-powered submarines is an historic and transformative endeavour for Australia. This whole-of-nation effort will transform Australia’s economic and national security landscape for decades to come.
The ASA’s Infrastructure Planning and Coordination (IP&C) Division is responsible for planning and coordinating the delivery of physical infrastructure that will:
  • Enable AUKUS partners to have a rotational presence at HMAS Stirling
  • Support Australia’s acquisition and sustainment of Virginia Class submarines
  • Deliver Australia’s sovereign build and sustainment of SSN-AUKUS submarines
In this role, you will use commercial, workforce, financial and business operations levers to improve organisational performance, strengthen delivery confidence and enable informed executive decision-making.
This position is eligible for an additional remuneration benefit known within ASA as a Building Capability Payment (BCP), applied in addition to base salary for critical capability disciplines.

About the Team
The Infrastructure Planning and Coordination (IP&C) Division coordinates the infrastructure that enables Australia’s nuclear-powered submarine capability. The work spans major programs and sites across Western Australia and South Australia, bringing together government, industry and international partners to deliver nationally significant outcomes.
You’ll join a collaborative, high-performing environment where you can shape strategy, influence delivery outcomes and contribute to one of Australia’s most complex infrastructure portfolios.

Key Responsibilities: 
You will be responsible for leading and enabling infrastructure operations outcomes, including:
  • Leading and growing high-performing teams, building capability and fostering a culture of accountability and collaboration
  • Driving continuous improvement across reporting, governance, information management and organisational performance
  • Providing strategic leadership and sound judgement to solve complex problems and balance competing priorities
  • Strengthening delivery confidence through robust performance oversight, insights and operational levers
  • Applying strong commercial, financial and business management acumen to translate data into decisions and action
  • Influencing outcomes across diverse stakeholder groups where success relies on collaboration rather than direct authority
  • Identifying and managing enterprise risks, opportunities and dependencies to improve delivery outcomes
  • Operating effectively in ambiguity, providing clear advice and direction in evolving environments
  • Preparing and delivering high-quality advice and communication to senior executives, government stakeholders and delivery partners
About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Proven leadership experience in complex operational, portfolio, program or infrastructure environments
  • Strong commercial, financial and business management capability
  • Experience improving organisational performance through governance, reporting and insight-led decision-making
  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes across multiple stakeholders and competing priorities
  • High-level written and verbal communication skills, with experience advising senior leaders
